Hi Elena —

Thanks for choosing Redwood. I'm Rachel (Sales Ops / Vendor Intake) — I own the supplier onboarding checklist for this deal. To keep things moving, can you share the initial company documents and confirm a 30–45 minute kickoff next week?

What we typically need from vendors to complete our vendor setup and enable PO issuance:
- Completed W-9 or W-8 (if US tax status differs)
- Legal entity name and DBAs (must match W-9)
- Bank details for ACH: bank name, account number, routing, and either a voided check or bank attestation
- Remit address for invoices (AP email/portal)
- Corporate contact for billing and contract questions
- Certificate of Insurance (COI) if annual spend is expected > $50k (we can discuss threshold)
- Any required compliance docs (SOC 2, data processing addenda) — helpful but not always required initially

I've attached our standard onboarding checklist to this thread (redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist_v1.pdf) to show the exact fields we'll route into Finance and Procurement. Two quick process notes:
- Standard PO term: Net 45 by default (we can discuss Net 30 for strategic partners)
- Redwood prefers ACH/EFT when possible; we can accept wire in special cases

Suggested kickoff slots (PT):
- Wed May 5, 10:00–10:30 AM
- Wed May 5, 2:00–2:30 PM
- Thu May 6, 1:00–1:30 PM

If you can reply with the W-9 and bank profile, we'll kick off Finance verification immediately. Feel free to send any vendor profile or intake form you've filled out already.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim

Rachel — quick answers from Sales/ops perspective:
- Consolidated monthly POs: Acceptable for supplier spend below $50k/month. We require each invoice line to reference the PO number or a PO range and the contract/order reference. For vendors expected to exceed $50k/month, we move to per-project or per-PO tracking.
- Bank verification: Finance will accept either a bank attestation letter on bank letterhead OR micro-deposit verification. If BlueOak prefers not to provide micro-deposits, ask for the bank letter and a voided check.

If BlueOak sends the W-9 + bank attestation, we can issue a provisional PO to allow initial work while Finance finishes EFT verification.

Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

Confirming Finance requirements:
- Legal name must match W-9 exactly. We will not activate bank ACH without either (a) micro-deposit verification completed and confirmed by Treasury, or (b) an official bank attestation letter plus a voided check.
- EFT enrollment form or vendor banking form preferred (signed), or a remittance/ACH onboarding form.
- Tax classification must be clear on the W-9; if foreign entity, escalate for W-8 processing.
- COI: not required for expected volumes under $50k annually, but please note higher thresholds or contractual requirements may trigger it later.

Action for Rachel: collect signed EFT/ACH form or bank letter + voided check and confirm legal entity string. We can then provision a provisional PO (up to $25k) while Treasury completes final verification (usually 3–5 business days).

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the W-9/profile. Per our internal review, here are the items we still need to complete onboarding and issue a provisional PO: 
- Signed EFT/ACH enrollment form OR a bank attestation letter on bank letterhead + voided check (one of these is required)
- Confirm legal entity exact string to match W-9 (please confirm if the DBA differs)
- Remittance AP contact and AP email for invoice submission

COI is not required at this stage given projected spend, and SOC 2 is optional (helpful to speed contract review but not mandatory for setup). Once we receive the bank verification and EFT form we can issue a provisional PO (up to $25k) within 24 hours; Treasury will complete final EFT verification in 3–5 business days.

Confirming our kickoff: Wed May 5 at 2:00 PM PT works for us — joining will be me (Rachel), Logan (AE), and Marcus (Finance). Meeting invite to follow.
